title: Daily interval writes report before planning
query: A Daily Interval automation calls interval-update for last_24h -> next_24h. What should it load, write, and avoid?
reference_points: Loads default goals, tickets, memory, Pulse reports, interval reports, and PM thread refs without the automation restating them
Uses the latest weekly_interval report as parent context when present
Writes a date-stamped .farplane/reports/interval/daily_interval/<timestamp>.md report before durable goals or ticket mutation
Does not select due jobs, update scheduler state, or perform broad strategy replanning

title: Weekly interval gates material goals deltas
query: The Weekly Interval review wants to change the north star and next-week priorities after reading daily reports. What gates apply?
reference_points: Loads farplane/goals.md plus daily_interval reports inside the review window
Labels missing or stale evidence as source gaps
Writes the interval report before mutating farplane/goals.md
Requires approval for north-star, KPI, strategy-axis, quarterly, yearly, or durable milestone changes
Routes executable changes into tickets or Goal Advisor handoffs

title: Interval extensions stay additive
query: A project automation calls interval-update with project_root, interval_id, windows, and one extra customer-doc ref. What should the automation include, and what should the skill resolve itself?
reference_points: Automation passes project_root, interval_id, review_window, planning_window, and additive extensions only
interval-update resolves default goals, tickets, memory, Pulse reports, interval reports, PM manifest, and report roots
Extensions may add context refs, phase instructions, lanes, or policy details
The automation should not restate every default Farplane path or gate
Project-specific profiles stay in automation prompts or project docs, not generic skill first-load refs

title: Interval reports are date-stamped
query: A weekly_interval run succeeds. Where should the report go and how should consumers find the newest one?
reference_points: Does not use latest.md as the canonical report
Consumers find the newest report by timestamp sorting or explicit links in subsequent reports
No tracked config or scheduler state is mutated just to store last_report
